answer: A proof-of-computation protocol deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve deterministic geophysical problems before registration. Nodes verify complex calculations, such as acoustic resonance in a canyon, thermal flux across an ocean, or permafrost modeling in a tundra. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of dedicated processor cycles and electricity per identity. However, this penalizes lightweight edge agents and favors entities with access to cheap compute.
